bias: Friday's late-session price action reads as a partial unwind rather than an escalation. The Treasury-demand story held exactly where it was -- three straight Note auctions with thin indirect demand, module still at Early Warning, no new auctions over the weekend to move it either way. But the acute bond-market stress that had pushed the 30Y through 5.5% and MOVE above 100 eased into the close: yields pulled back 2.5-4.1bp across the belly/long end, the 30Y ended back under the 5.5% stress line, and MOVE dropped -8.2% to 96.00. None of the standard confirmation channels ever joined in the first place -- credit stayed calm, funding stayed normal, the dollar was flat, and equities (including Asia) firmed further. On top of that, the one new structural data point (H.8's Sep 16 bank-demand vintage) ticked down only marginally (-0.19% w/w). Taken together, this looks like a rates-market repricing that has, for now, stopped short of the long-end stress line rather than one that broke through it and kept going. The open question into next week is whether Monday's session holds these calmer levels or reopens the selloff.

counterargs.read: The weight of Friday's own closing evidence favors de-escalation over confirmation: the specific technical trigger this framework was watching (30Y > 5.5%) is no longer active, and the move to get there partially reversed within the same session on a MOVE decline. But the underlying auction-demand weakness (three straight thin-indirect prints) and the fresh dip in bank Treasury demand are still live, unresolved threads with no new print this weekend to clear them. The right read is to keep the Treasury module at Early Warning -- unchanged, not downgraded -- while treating the long-end breach as a within-session event rather than a new steady state, and to watch whether Monday holds Friday's closing levels.

treasury_auctions.narrative: The 7Y (91282CRM5, Sep 24) settled decently on the metrics that matter most for dealer stress: BTC 2.42 and dealer take-down 10.76%, both roughly in line with the two comparable 7Y prints in the ledger (Aug 27: BTC 2.50/dealer 10.84%; Jul 28: BTC 2.49/dealer 11.7%). But indirect demand was again soft at 49.13% -- below both those comps (53.72%, 63.0%) and in the same range as the Sep 22 2Y (49.27%) and Sep 23 5Y (46.98%). That makes three straight Note auctions with thinning indirect (often foreign/end-investor) demand, even though only the 5Y also showed elevated dealer take-down. The module holds at EARLY WARNING: this is not a third weak print on every metric (no escalation to Intermediation Stress), but it is not a clean auction either (no downgrade to Healthy). Separately from the auction story, US10Y and US30Y kept selling off into today's session (+11.1bp/+11.7bp since the prior run), with the 30Y crossing the 5.5% long-end stress line for the first time and MOVE spiking a further +9.6% to 104.58. Funding remains normal (SOFR-IORB -2bp, repo_confirmation false) and credit is calm, so this stays short of Intermediation Stress. The next test is the H.8 bank-demand read today and whether credit or equities start reacting to the long end above 5.5%.

transmission.bottom_line: Friday's close looks like a partial unwind of the day's own stress episode rather than an escalation. The Treasury-demand story is exactly where it was -- three straight thin-indirect Note auctions, module at Early Warning, no new print this weekend to move it -- and a new H.8 vintage shows bank demand ticking down a modest -0.19% w/w. But the acute bond-market stress eased: the 30Y closed back under 5.5%, MOVE fell -8.2% to below 100, and every other transmission channel -- credit, funding, USD, and both US and Asian equities -- stayed calm-to-firm throughout. Treat 'Long-End Stress Confirmed' as no longer active on today's levels while keeping the underlying auction-demand and bank-demand softness on watch. The next test is whether Monday's session holds Friday's calmer levels or reopens the selloff.
